name: US inflation
summary: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October after 3.7% annual inflation in September, inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band
state: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above forecasts, after 0.6% in September, with energy up 0.7% and shelter 0.3% (ABC News, 10 Nov). The BLS put annual inflation at 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August; an October annual rate cannot be calculated because no CPI was collected in October 2025 during the shutdown (FRED). Index levels imply a rate of roughly 3.9–4.1%, inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band and rising since July. November CPI is due in mid-December.
for_you: Households on fixed incomes and renters are most exposed as prices rise faster than the 2% target. Borrowers on variable rates are exposed to higher interest costs if the Fed raises rates in December.
rubric_hit: CPI 3.7% (Sep) and about 4% (Oct est.) in 3.0–4.5% Watch band, rising 3 months

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.
